column3: C reads uninit stack residue for len>4 (verifier stress test); Rust zero-inits stack_buf — deterministic refinement, test contract only exercises len=4
LLVM folds C source !(data+thoff) null-check to !data (ptr-provenance); Rust checks data+thoff faithfully — diverges only for skb->data==0 && thoff!=0, a NULL packet pointer the kernel never produces
C deliberately returns uninit stack residue array[9] (verifier-coverage test); Rust zero-inits the array — deterministic refinement, same class as test_stack_var_off

deliberate translation divergence (documented in test_core_reloc_type_based.rs): scripts/type_id.py lowers only TYPE_ID_TARGET, not the TYPE_EXISTS/MATCHES/SIZE relocations this test uses (#45), so the translation implements the C source's own #else fallback branch (data.skip = true) while the C object compiles the #if branch with real TYPE_EXISTS/MATCHES/SIZE relocations; the runtime harness honors data.skip

deliberate translation divergence (documented in test_ctx.rs): C guards the counter with bpf_in_hardirq(), which reads the weak percpu ksym __preempt_count (or pcpu_hot behind a CO-RE field-exists check) via this_cpu_ptr; not translated yet (#47), and the probe only ever runs from the hardirq callback it is named for — the guard is always true there, so Rust bumps unconditionally

deliberate translation divergence (documented in fexit_bpf2bpf.rs): the target subprogram's `val` parameter is constant-propagated away by the target object's LLVM, so the trampoline ctx layout the C object assumes differs from the translation's; the harness attaches and validates at runtime

C-object CO-RE bug, not a translation divergence: BPF_CORE_WRITE_BITFIELD(&md.u.md2, ...) computes p = &md.u.md2 + BYTE_OFFSET, but LLVM roots the relo spec at erspan_metadata (access "0:1:1:7"), so libbpf patches BYTE_OFFSET to 11 and the C writes land at md+14/md+15 — past the 12-byte struct — leaving md2 all-zero in the set_tunnel_opt payload; Rust writes the bits at their real offsets

deliberate translation divergence (documented in syscall.rs header): the C statics are full 168-byte `union bpf_attr` objects while the translation uses right-sized prefix structs (btf_load_attr 24B, prog_load_attr 40B, map_update_attr 24B) — byte-compatible for the attr_size each call passes, but the checker compares the whole named global, so the bytes that exist only in C's union tail have no counterpart; additionally C's `raw_btf` is a stack local whose address goes into btf_load_attr.btf, where the translation makes it a static
